posts.title: The Price of a Lesson
posts.description: At fourteen, I stole a pair of trousers and some socks. We could not afford them. I thought if I could reach the street, I might look like any other boy. The shopkeeper caught me at the door. He looked at my shirt, then at my feet. He said he felt sorry for me. Then he asked what else I had. I turned my pockets inside out. A few coins. He waited. posts.title: The Freedom to Meander
posts.description: While in Athens, I have noticed something about the way I explore the city. When I go out alone, I often end up in more interesting places than I had planned to visit. Sometimes, I had no plan to begin with. I simply walk, notice something, change direction, and keep going. One place leads to another. Curiosity decides the next turn. posts.title: Ancients Ad Infinitum
posts.description: So, historians observe, an age Hath older ages on its page; And these have older worlds within ’em, And so proceed ad infinitum. And we shall be the ancients, too, To future eyes that look us through; And those have later eyes to view ’em, And so again, ad infinitum.
